subject: chemistry

moments.title: Cosmic ray N-14
moments.body: Korff discovers cosmic-ray neutrons produce 14C from atmospheric 14N. The radioactive isotope (half-life 5,730 years) mixes through the biosphere.
moments.takeaway: A natural radioisotope is continuously made in the atmosphere.

moments.title: Libby develops radiocarbon dating
moments.body: Libby measures 14C in biological samples and calibrates against tree rings. Living things have a known 14C content; dead samples lose it predictably. 1960 Nobel.

moments.title: Dead Sea Scrolls dated
moments.body: Radiocarbon dating confirms the Dead Sea Scrolls are 2,000 years old. Public attention on the technique surges.

moments.title: AMS dating
moments.body: AMS measures 14C atom by atom, needing milligrams instead of grams. Iceman 'Ötzi' is dated (~5,300 years). Even microscopic samples can now be dated.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Radiocarbon underpins prehistoric archaeology, climate science, art authentication, forensic medicine. The 'bomb spike' from 1950s nuclear tests is a globally calibrated marker.
now.open_questions: Can carbon-cycle changes due to fossil fuels still allow accurate dating beyond 2050?

reflection: Radiocarbon dating disproved many cultural origin stories; revealed Shroud of Turin as medieval. How do communities respond when chemistry contradicts their narratives?
